title: google_web_search loops indefinitely when no relevant results are found

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue is a valid and actionable bug report detailing how `google_web_search` enters an infinite loop when queries yield no relevant results, complete with reproduction steps, environment context, and expected behavior.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix requires adding search attempt tracking or a maximum search attempt limit in `packages/core/src/tools/web-search.ts` to prevent unbounded search iterations when no relevant results are found. This is a localized logic fix in a single source file.

summary.problem: The google_web_search tool repeatedly reformulates and retries search queries when no relevant results are found, entering an unbounded loop.
summary.root_cause: WebSearchTool lacks attempt tracking or bounding logic for search requests, and loop detection based on exact argument hashes fails to trigger when search queries are slightly reformulated.
summary.context: When requesting obscure or unindexed information, the agent continuously generates altered search queries and calls google_web_search indefinitely until manually interrupted by the user.

steps: Track search execution count or consecutive search attempts within WebSearchTool or its invocation context.
Enforce a configurable maximum search attempt threshold when queries return no relevant results or citations.
Return an informative response when the attempt threshold is reached, instructing the model to inform the user that no results were found instead of making further search calls.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Web search limits consecutive search attempts when queries return no results and returns an explicit stopping message once the limit is reached.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in packages/core/src/tools/web-search.test.ts verifying search attempt tracking across invocations.
Verify that exceeding the maximum attempt limit returns a prompt advising the model to stop searching and report results to the user.
